question: A vending machine had 25 dollars in coins collected at the start of the day. A refund for a jammed snack took out 20 dollars. A busy lunch rush then added 31 more dollars. A restocking bonus from the vendor multiplied the coin total by 5. Finally, the machine's monthly maintenance fee took out 12 dollars. A separate vending machine down the hall, unrelated to this one, collected 90 dollars that day. How many dollars were left in the machine's coin total?

A food bank had 184 cans of vegetables in its emergency stockpile. A matching grant multiplied the stockpile by 5. A small donation added 3 more cans. A distribution event then removed 123 cans for families in need. A grocery store partnership added 80 more cans. A citywide drive then multiplied the stockpile by 4. Finally, a last delivery added 25 more cans. A separate stockpile at a nearby shelter, unrelated to this one, held 600 cans. How many cans were in the tracked stockpile?

Ana tracked the total number of trading cards in her binder all season, starting with 84 cards. Her rival collector, Beto, had a binder holding half a dozen fewer cards than hers to start, though this story only follows Ana's binder. A booster box opening tripled her card count. A trade show then multiplied her tracked total by 5. She then split her whole collection evenly across 4 binders, and from then on only tracked the first binder's count. Finally, a birthday gift added 58 more cards to that first binder. How many cards were in Ana's tracked binder by the end of the season?

A small nonprofit tracked the total dollars in its emergency relief fund all year, starting with 13 dollars carried over from last year. A single large donation added 72 dollars. A matching challenge then doubled the fund. A corporate sponsor multiplied the fund by 8. A bake sale added 21 more dollars. A separate scholarship fund at the same nonprofit, unrelated to this one, held 1000 dollars. Finally, a major relief payout took 828 dollars out of the emergency fund. How many dollars were left in the emergency relief fund?

A comic book shop had 54 issues of a rare series on the shelf. A collector bought 27 of them in one visit. A surprise reprint then doubled the remaining stock. A distributor delivery added 49 more issues. A damaged batch removed 2 issues. A convention order then multiplied the stock by 7. A second convention order multiplied the stock by 7 again. A separate rare comics case, unrelated to this series, held 120 issues. How many issues of the series were on the shelf after both convention orders?

A tailor tracked the total yards of fabric on the bolt, starting with 56 yards. A custom order used up 10 yards. A second order used another 7 yards. A dozen new patterns were designed that week, though that number has nothing to do with the fabric count. The tailor then converted the remaining fabric into a per-suit count, multiplying the tracked number by 9 suits' worth of fabric equivalence — a simple unit change. A wholesale order then multiplied that tracked count by 3. How many suit-equivalents did the tracked count come to?

Farmer Ito tracked the total pounds of apples in his orchard's storage barn, starting with 43 pounds already picked. His neighbor, farmer Kwan, had a barn holding 900 pounds that season, far more than Ito's, but only Ito's barn is tracked here. A morning harvest added 77 more pounds. A bumper crop then tripled the tracked total. An afternoon pick added 38 more pounds. A cold-storage recount, converting from pounds to crates for shipping — a simple unit change — multiplied the tracked count by 8 crates' worth. Finally, a shipment out removed 863 from the tracked crate count. How many crates were left in Ito's tracked storage?

A city's public library tracked the total number of ebook checkouts on its app, starting with 111 checkouts logged in week one. A viral book club recommendation quadrupled the checkout count. A follow-up feature on a podcast multiplied it by 8 more. A steady trickle of new checkouts added 44 more. A holiday promotion multiplied the checkout count by 8 again. A system glitch then wrongly counted 14102 checkouts that had to be removed. Finally, a correction added back 21 checkouts. How many checkouts did the tracked count show after the correction?

Chef Marco tracked the total number of dumplings prepped for the dinner rush, starting with 180 dumplings ready at opening. His sous-chef, Elena, was separately prepping appetizers, having made 60 of them by then, but only Marco's dumpling count is tracked here. By midmorning, half of the dumplings were set aside for a private event, and only that private-event batch was tracked from then on. By midday, each of those dumplings was found to actually be a bundle of 7 once unwrapped for plating, multiplying the tracked count. By afternoon, a catering order multiplied the tracked count by 8. By evening, a second catering order multiplied it by 8 again. By night, a final banquet order multiplied the tracked count by 9. How many dumplings did the tracked count show by night?

A juice stand tracked the total ounces of lemonade in its cooler, starting with 16 ounces left over from yesterday. A big batch multiplied the cooler's tracked volume by 7. A fresh pitcher added 24 more ounces. Another pitcher added 15 more ounces. The stand owner also converted her pricing from cents to dollars on the menu board, a simple unit change unrelated to the lemonade volume. A separate water cooler nearby, unrelated to this one, held 200 ounces. Finally, one more pitcher added 17 more ounces. How many ounces of lemonade were in the tracked cooler?

A pharmacy tracked the total number of pills in a large stock bottle, starting with 187 pills. A morning prescription used 117 pills. A second prescription used 9 more. A third prescription used 15 more. The pharmacist then repackaged the remainder into 5-pill blister packs, multiplying the tracked count by 5 to get the individual pill count across all packs combined for the inventory system — converting from bottle count to blister-pack count, a simple unit change. A separate stock bottle, unrelated to this one, held 400 pills. How many pills did the tracked blister-pack inventory show?

Baker Yuki tracked the total number of croissants baked for a wedding order, starting with 227 croissants from the first batch. Her assistant baker, Marcus, was separately preparing 90 cupcakes for the same event, but only Yuki's croissant count is tracked here. A second batch tripled the tracked croissant count. A quality check then removed 446 croissants that didn't rise properly. A third batch doubled what remained. An extra tray added 8 more croissants. Yuki then converted her tracking from individual croissants to dozens-boxes for delivery, multiplying the tracked count by 8 boxes' worth — a simple unit change. Finally, a last-minute tray added 7 more to the tracked count. How many did the tracked delivery count come to?

Jordan tracked the total dollars in his food truck's register, starting with 43 dollars at opening. His business partner, Casey, kept a separate register for the dessert cart, which started with 90 dollars, but only Jordan's register is tracked here. A morning supply run took out 32 dollars. A lunch rush then added 67 dollars. Jordan also converted his tip total from coins to whole dollars for easier counting, a simple unit change. An afternoon slow spell then meant a refund of 63 dollars had to be given back. Finally, an evening rush added 70 more dollars. How many dollars were in Jordan's register by the end of the evening?

Mateo tracked the total dollars in his skateboard fund, starting with 142 dollars saved. His friend Diego, by comparison, had saved a mere half of that in his own separate fund, but only Mateo's fund is tracked here. A parking fee mishap cost Mateo 1 dollar. A birthday gift added 25 dollars. A big purchase of new wheels then cost 147 dollars from the tracked fund. Finally, a summer job quadrupled whatever remained in the fund. How much money was in Mateo's skateboard fund after the summer job?

Officer Reyes tracked the total number of parking tickets issued downtown, starting with 223 tickets already issued that week. Officer Nolan, working uptown, had issued 90 tickets separately, but only Reyes's downtown count is tracked here. On Monday, 31 more tickets were issued. On Tuesday, 153 tickets were voided after a city amnesty. On Wednesday, 26 more tickets were issued. On Thursday, 53 tickets were voided in a second amnesty wave. On Friday, a citywide crackdown multiplied the tracked ticket count by 9. Over the weekend, a holiday enforcement push multiplied it by 5 more. How many tickets did the tracked downtown count show by the end of the weekend?

A print shop had 109 flyers ready for a client on Monday. A reprint request multiplied the flyer count by 5. A second client's matching order multiplied it by 8. The flyers were then split evenly among 5 delivery routes, and only the first route's flyer count was tracked from then on. A separate print job for another client, unrelated to this order, produced 300 flyers. Finally, a damaged batch removed 162 flyers from the tracked route's count. How many flyers were in the tracked route's count?

Maya tracked the total dollars in her jar of birthday money, starting with 82 dollars on the morning of her party. Her twin brother, Leo, had a separate jar that started the day with 150 dollars, but only Maya's jar is tracked here. During the party, a group of cousins gave her 77 more dollars. Later that afternoon, a grandparent added 29 more dollars. That evening, Maya spent 127 dollars on a new bike. The next morning, she spent another 37 dollars on accessories for it. How many dollars were left in Maya's jar?

A juice company tracked the total liters of orange juice in its production tank, starting with 125 liters. A morning press added 49 more liters. A second press then tripled the tank's tracked volume. A bottling run removed 402 liters from the tank. The remaining juice was then split evenly between two tanks, and only the first tank's volume was tracked. A concentrate additive multiplied the tracked tank's volume by 5. Finally, the company converted its tracked volume from liters to gallons for the export label — a simple unit change — after splitting the shipment evenly between two export containers, and tracked only the first container's amount. How many gallons did the tracked export container show?

Coach Diallo tracked the total minutes his relay team ran in practice, starting with 155 minutes logged already. His assistant coach, Farah, separately tracked the sprint team's minutes, which totaled half that amount, but only Diallo's relay team is tracked here. A morning session added 43 more minutes. An afternoon session added 57 more minutes. An evening session added 18 more minutes. Finally, an injury forced the team to cut 163 minutes of planned practice from the tracked total. How many minutes did Diallo's tracked total show?

A bookstore had 225 copies of a bestselling novel in its warehouse. A reprint order doubled the warehouse's stock. A small delivery added 34 more copies. A big chain order then took 364 copies out of the warehouse. The remaining copies were split evenly among 5 branch stores, and only the flagship branch's share was tracked from then on. A separate warehouse across town, unrelated to this stock, held 900 copies of a different book. Finally, a return shipment added 45 more copies to the flagship branch's tracked share. How many copies were in the flagship branch's tracked share?

Manager Torres tracked the total inventory units in Warehouse C, starting with 126 units. Her regional counterpart, manager Blake, tracked Warehouse D separately, which held 5000 units, but only Warehouse C is tracked here. A supplier tripled the warehouse's tracked stock. A second supplier's shipment multiplied it by 7 more. A small local order added 25 more units. A massive wholesale order then removed 1053 units from the tracked stock. A restock then multiplied the tracked count by 5. Finally, a merger with a smaller distributor tripled the tracked count once more. How many units did Warehouse C's tracked count show after the merger?

Photographer Lena tracked the total number of photos on her camera's memory card, starting with 181 photos from the morning shoot. Her assistant, Marco, had a separate card with 90 photos, but only Lena's card is tracked here. A batch deletion of blurry shots removed 131 photos. A further cleanup removed 5 more. A second shoot added 16 more photos. A quick test shot added 10 more. Finally, Lena merged nine identical burst sequences into the count, multiplying her tracked total by 9. How many photos were on Lena's tracked memory card after the merge?

A juice bar tracked the total ounces of smoothie mix in its blender pitcher, starting with 48 ounces. The mix was split evenly into 6 identical cups, and only the first cup's ounces were tracked from then on. A refill then multiplied the tracked cup's ounces by 6. Half of that cup was then poured into a to-go container, and only the to-go container's ounces were tracked. A dozen straws were stocked that day, though that number has nothing to do with the smoothie amount. A spill then lost 19 ounces from the tracked container. The bar owner also converted her price list from cents to dollars, a simple unit change unrelated to the smoothie. A separate blender across the counter, unrelated to this pitcher, held 100 ounces. Finally, a triple-size upgrade multiplied the tracked container's ounces by 3. How many ounces were in the tracked to-go container after the upgrade?

A school tracked the total number of canned goods collected for its food drive, starting with 105 cans on day one. Day two's collection added 31 more cans. Day three's collection added 50 more cans. A matching donor then multiplied the tracked total by 6. The cans were then repackaged into cases of 6, and the tracked number became the case count instead. A late donation added 52 more cases. Finally, a shipping error removed 37 cases from the tracked total. How many cases did the tracked total show at the end of the drive?

A vending business tracked the total dollars in Machine 4's coin box, starting with 45 dollars. A morning refill of change added 56 more dollars. An afternoon cash pickup removed 60 dollars. An evening top-up added 10 more dollars. A refund for a stuck item removed 43 dollars. Finally, a late-night sale added 12 more dollars. Machine 7, unrelated to this box, held 300 dollars. How many dollars were in Machine 4's coin box by the end of the night?
